name: application-amenity-request-row
title: Amenity Request Row
description: Hotel amenity/service request list with an icon, room and request label, elapsed time, and a status pill (Pending, In progress, Complete, Cancelled).
useWhen: Showing a hotel staff queue of guest service requests (towels, room service, late checkout, maintenance) with their current status.
You need a compact, scannable list rather than one detailed request at a time.
The four-state status vocabulary (Pending/In progress/Complete/Cancelled) matches your workflow as-is.
avoidWhen: You're showing an internal access/permission approval, not a guest-facing service request — use `approval-request-card` for that unrelated context.
Your workflow needs different or additional states — extend the status map rather than force-fitting these four labels.
Only one request needs to be shown in detail — a single card reads better than a one-item list.
responsiveBehavior: Single-column list at a fixed max width; each row stays a fixed icon–text–pill layout, with the label truncating before the pill ever wraps or shrinks.
accessibility: Status is conveyed through both the pill's text label and its color, never color alone, so it reads correctly without color vision.
Each icon is aria-hidden since the adjacent text label already names the request type; the icon is a visual accelerator, not the sole label.
Rows are marked up as a <ul>/<li> list so assistive tech announces the item count and position, not a series of unrelated divs.

variants.title: Amenity Request Row
variants.description: Four requests (towels, room service, late checkout, maintenance) across Pending/In progress/Complete/Cancelled states.
accessibility: Each of the four statuses uses a distinct hue (amber/blue/emerald/red) reserved for that state only, never reused for a different meaning.

variants.title: Amenity Request Row (Dark)
variants.description: Amenity request row adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Status pills use low-opacity tinted backgrounds with their -400 text step to hold WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface.
